why: A is Theorem 5.2 and (4_λ) in singular homology for any monotone ℕ-filtration X_0 ⊆ X_1 ⊆ … of subsets whose steps k < n have finite-dimensional homology (arbitrary dimensions). C_λ is Σ_k dim H_λ(X_{k+1},X_k), or the number of p ∈ P with ind p = λ under a cell hypothesis. A also has the finiteness of H_*(X_n,X_0). B is the special case of a Fin-indexed chain ∅ = X_0 ⊆ … ⊆ X_k = X whose steps are single cells (homology F in degree λ_i, 0 otherwise): weak inequalities, χ equality (finsums) and (4_λ). A ⇒ B: extend the chain to a monotone ℕ-filtration (Glue.exists_nat_filtration) and apply singular_morse_inequality_of_cells (strong), le_of_altSum_le (weak), and singular_euler_characteristic with N = max λ_i together with the project's singularMorseNumber_eq_card. Vanishing above N turns the finsums into finite sums; k = 0 is handled separately. B ⇒ A fails: B only covers cell-like steps, and has no finiteness statement for general filtrations.
